'''Robert Everett Ecke''' is an American experimental physicist who is a laboratory fellow and director emeritus of the Center for Nonlinear Studies (CNLS) at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Center for Nonlinear Studies |url=https://cnls.lanl.gov/external/people/Robert_Ecke.php |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=cnls.lanl.gov}}</ref> and Affiliate Professor of Physics at the [[University of Washington]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Robert Ecke {{!}} Department of Physics {{!}} University of Washington |url=https://phys.washington.edu/people/robert-ecke |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=phys.washington.edu}}</ref> His research has included chaotic [[nonlinear dynamics]], [[pattern formation]], rotating [[Rayleigh-Bénard convection]], two-dimensional [[turbulence]], [[granular materials]], and [[stratified flows]].<ref name=":0" /> He is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS)<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> and of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS),<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Elected Fellows {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/listing |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=www.aaas.org |language=en}}</ref> was chair of the APS Topical Group on Statistical and Nonlinear Physics,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Executive Committee – Unit – GSNP |url=https://engage.aps.org/gsnp/governance/executive-committee/past-officers |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=engage.aps.org}}</ref> served in numerous roles in the APS Division of Fluid Dynamics, and was the Secretary of the Physics Section of the AAAS.

== Education and early life ==
Ecke was born in Los Angeles, California, in February 1953. He grew up in [[Helena, Montana]] and graduated from the [[University of Washington]] in 1975 with a B.S. in Physics<ref name=":0" /> (with Distinction) and [[Phi Beta Kappa]]. He received his PhD in physics, also from the [[University of Washington]],<ref name=":0" /> under [[J. Gregory Dash]] in 1982 studying [[Kosterlitz-Thouless]] melting in low-temperature helium monolayers on [[graphite]].

== Career and research ==
After a brief postdoctoral research position with Oscar Vilches at [[University of Washington]], he became a Director's Funded Postdoctoral Fellow<ref name=":0" /> with [[John Wheatley (physicist)|John Wheatley]] at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] in fall of 1983 where he pursued cryogenic convection and [[Chaos theory|chaotic]] dynamics. He became a technical staff member in the Condensed Matter and Thermal Physics Group of the Physics Division in 1986<ref name=":0" /> where he did research on chaos and nonlinear dynamics in [[Rayleigh-Bénard convection]] of a [[helium-3|<sup>3</sup>He]]-[[superfluid helium-4|superfluid <sup>4</sup>He]] mixture<ref>{{cite journal |author1=H. Haucke |author2=R.E. Ecke |year=1987 |title=Mode-locking and chaos in Rayleigh-Bénard convection |journal=Physica D |volume=25 |issue=1–3 |pages=307–329 |doi=10.1016/0167-2789(87)90106-0|bibcode=1987PhyD...25..307H }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=R. Mainieri |author2=T.S. Sullivan |author3=R.E. Ecke |year=1989 |title=Two-parameter study of the quasiperiodic route to chaos in convecting 3He-superfluid-4He mixtures |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |volume=63 |issue=21 |pages=2357–2360 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.63.2357|pmid=10040868 }}</ref> and on pattern formation in rotating convection and in compositional convection.   Later, he studied turbulence in [[Rayleigh-Bénard convection]] with<ref>{{cite journal |author1=R.E. Ecke |author2=F. Zhong |author3=E. Knobloch |year=1992 |title=Hopf Bifurcation with Broken Reflection Symmetry in Rotating Rayleigh-Bénard Convection |journal=Europhys. Lett. |volume=19 |issue=3 |pages=177–182 |doi=10.1209/0295-5075/19/3/005|bibcode=1992EL.....19..177E |s2cid=250856323 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=F. Zhong |author2=R.E. Ecke |author3=V. Steinberg |year=1993 |title=Rotating Rayleigh–Bénard convection: Asymmetric modes and vortex states |journal=J. Fluid Mech. |volume=249 |pages=135–159 |doi=10.1017/S0022112093001119|bibcode=1993JFM...249..135Z |s2cid=120365397 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=Y. Liu |author2=R.E. Ecke |year=1997 |title=Heat Transport Scaling in Turbulent Rayleigh-Bénard Convection: Effects of Rotation and Prandtl Number |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |volume=79 |issue=12 |pages=2257–2260 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.79.2257|bibcode=1997PhRvL..79.2257L }}</ref> and without rotation and pattern formation in high-pressure gaseous convection, including experiments on spiral defect chaos.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=D.A. Egolf |author2=I.V. Melnikov |author3=W. Pesch |author4=R.E. Ecke |year=2000 |title=Mechanisms of extensive spatiotemporal chaos in Rayleigh–Bénard convection |journal=Nature |volume=404 |issue=6779 |pages=733–736 |doi=10.1038/35008013|pmid=10783880 |bibcode=2000Natur.404..733E |s2cid=4346527 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=R.E. Ecke |author2=Y. Hu |author3=R. Mainieri |author4=G. Ahlers |year=1995 |title=Excitation of Spirals and Chiral Symmetry Breaking in Rayleigh-Bénard Convection |journal=Science |volume=269 |issue=5231 |pages=1704–1707 |doi=10.1126/science.269.5231.1704|pmid=17821641 |bibcode=1995Sci...269.1704E |s2cid=30308034 }}</ref> In 1997, he was appointed to the position of Laboratory Fellow<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Energy |first=Los Alamos National Laboratory, Operated by Los Alamos National Security, LLC, for the U. S. Department of |title=Fellows Directory |url=https://www.lanl.gov/collaboration/fellows/directory.php |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=www.lanl.gov |language=en}}</ref> and continued to expand his research into two-dimensional [[turbulence]],<ref>{{cite journal |author1=S. Chen |author2=R.E. Ecke |author3=G.L. Eyink |author4=M. Rivera |author5=M. Wan |author6=Z. Xiao |year=2006 |title=Physical Mechanism of the Two-Dimensional Inverse Energy Cascade |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |volume=96 |issue=8 |article-number=084502 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.084502|pmid=16606186 |bibcode=2006PhRvL..96h4502C }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=G. Boffettta |author2=R.E. Ecke |year=2012 |title=Two-Dimensional Turbulence |journal=Annu. Rev. Fluid Mech. |volume=44 |issue=1 |pages=427–451 |doi=10.1146/annurev-fluid-120710-101240|bibcode=2012AnRFM..44..427B |url=https://www.openaccessrepository.it/record/141717 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241213135003/https://www.openaccessrepository.it//record/141717 |archive-date=December 13, 2024 |url-access=subscription |doi-access=free }}</ref> granular chain dynamics, granular media dynamics, stick-slip motion in an earthquake experiment, solutal convection,<ref>{{cite journal |author1=S. Backhaus |author2=K. Turitsyn |author3=R.E. Ecke |year=2011 |title=Convective Instability and Mass Transport of Diffusion Layers in a Hele-Shaw Geometry |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |volume=106 |issue=10 |article-number=104501 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.104501|pmid=21469794 |arxiv=1011.4619 |bibcode=2011PhRvL.106j4501B |doi-access=free }}</ref> and turbulent mixing in stratified flows. In 2004, he became the director of the Center for Nonlinear Studies, where he directed research on [[condensed matter physics]], [[quantum information]], [[information science]], non-equilibrium and nonlinear physics, [[biophysics]], and [[computational chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Center for Nonlinear Studies |url=https://cnls.lanl.gov/external/History.php |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=cnls.lanl.gov}}</ref> Robert Ecke has published more than 110 research articles and has an [[h-index]] of 43 with 5400 citations<ref>{{Cite web |title=Robert Ecke |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=kAqXUGMAAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> according to his [[Google Scholar]] profile.
